hook_text: In 1375, a map maker in Spain drew an African king on his map, holding a giant gold nugget. Who was he?
clip_script: His name was Mansa Musa, ruler of Mali, and Europeans had never seen him. But they had heard. Mali stretched two thousand kilometres across West Africa, bigger than any kingdom in Europe. It controlled the gold that ended up in Europe's coins. Its king kept every nugget found in the empire. Its roads were so safe that a Moroccan traveller wrote that nobody feared robbers. It all began with Sundiata, the Lion of Mali, who could not walk as a child and grew up to found an empire. A century later, Mansa Musa ruled at its peak, and his fame travelled so far that a European map maker drew him in gold.
visual_style: A whiteboard Catalan-style map unrolling, a crowned king holding a gold nugget appearing over West Africa; the empire's outline spreading from the Atlantic to the Niger bend; a lion symbol for Sundiata.
pacing: Mystery hook, sweeping facts, a lion-hearted origin story.
